recipes.name: Broccoli Rice Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Gather ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 3-quart baking dish.
Place broccoli and 2 tablespoons water in a large microwave-safe bowl; cover with plastic wrap and microwave on high for 5 minutes, stirring once. Drain; transfer to a bowl.
Meanwhile, melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add celery, onion, and garlic; cook and stir until tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in condensed soups and milk; heat through.
Stir cooked vegetable-soup mixture into broccoli.
Stir in shredded cheese, mustard, paprika, and black pepper.
Stir in rice until combined. Transfer to the prepared baking dish.
Combine panko with remaining 1 tablespoon  melted butter; sprinkle on top casserole.
Bake in the preheated oven until browned and bubbly, 30 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli Rice Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This comforting broccoli rice casserole combines broccoli, rice, and a creamy cheese sauce, topped with crispy panko, baked until golden and bubbly.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe but way more work than needed. I cut up the velveeta into chunks and placed them in my casserole dish. Then I poured in the two cans of soup and 3/4 c. milk. I put the casserole dish in the oven at 350 and let the cheese melt. Once it was melted, I took the casserole dish out of the oven, stirred the contents until well mixed and added the rice, broccoli, and chopped onion..I omitted the celery. I cooked it for about 30 minutes on 350. It was a big hit.

I found the original recipe using the Wayback Machine. Here are the ingredients: 2 (10 ounce) packages frozen chopped broccoli; 3 cups instant rice; 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup; 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup; 1 ¼ cups water; 1 (16 ounce) package processed American cheese, cubed, 1 tablespoon butter; 1 bunch celery, chopped; 1 large onion, chopped; salt and pepper to taste I make this every Thanksgiving and everyone loves it, but I always tweak it to give it some more flavor!

I made this for dinner tonight (with a few changes based on what I had). I used basmati rice, fresh broccoli, fresh baby portabella mushrooms, onions, red peppers, three garlic cloves and grated a block of extra sharp cheddar. I had one large can of cream of mushroom soup. 

I sauteed the onions and peppers in olive oil to cook out some of the moisture and add flavour depth. The mushrooms, I sliced and cooked in olive oil and seasoned with a bit of salt and thyme. Next I put the soup in a pot, added some hot water and a couple tbsp of milk whisked it together over low heat and then whisked in the cheddar. I also added a dollop of mushroom base by Better than Bullion to give it a boost. Add the chopped fresh broccoli florets, stir coating them. Added in the onions, peppers and 2 cups rice until all is coated. Poured it all into a casserole dish, covered with foil and baked for 45 min on 410 degrees. Removed the foil and baked another 10 minutes, removed from oven & let stand for 10-15 minutes and then served. It was a big hit & seconds were had all around. 

My biggest advice is to season at each step of cooking. Those layers add up to a great and complex casserole.

For my very first broccoli rice & cheese casserole, I loved it.

I will give it 5 stars, but really didn't make it as written. It was a good reference. I used 2 small heads of fresh broccoli and a couple of diced carrots, which I steamed. Sauteed 1/2 of a yellow onion and 1 celery stalk with 1 clove of garlic. Mixed all that together with 2 cups (and a little...end of the box) of Minute rice, one can of cream of mushroom soup, and 2 1/2 cups of homemade chicken stock. Added an 8 oz block of Muenster, grated, and about 1/2 cup of grated parmesan cheese. Stirred it all together in a casserole dish and baked at 350 for about 50 mins total, stirring a couple of times through.

I steamed the broccoli, celery & onion in the steamer portion of my rice cooker while the rice cooked to perfection.

I chose to use Rico's spicy nacho cheese sauce 'cause the dish is a 'bland' dish and i prefer spicy and it worked out great! I also added a chopped red bell pepper for color, by the way.

The next time I make it I'll use brown rice for more fiber and less bland; however, in either case it's a great side dish. I may also try it as a main entrée with chicken breasts chunks and a bit of teriyaki sauce to spice it up a bit too.

First off- absolutely not bland!
This is a holiday staple and there are a ton of variations out there but this recipe is as close to perfect as it gets.
The three cups if rice is three cups if cooked rice, not raw resulting in six cups. That mistake would truly make it bland.
The trick with this casserole is that it should be soupy before baking so that the final result is not dry. The only essential that I add is a can or two of diced water chestnuts.
I saute the celery and onion in butter in a huge skillet, then add in soups, cheese and water. Nuke the broccoli a little, cook the rice in an instant pot. Then mix in the broccoli, rice and chestnuts and pour all in to casserole dish and bake for the 45 minutes. Top with cheese and sometimes some panko bread crumbs. Great recipe that has nice flavor without being overpowering.

I made it this way, 2 cups of white rice, 2 packages of frozen broccoli florets, onion and celery, cooked in 4 tablespoons of butter, added 3 tablespoons of flour, cooked that 4minutes, then added 2 1/2 cups of half/half and cooked until thickened. Added 1 can of cream of mushroom soup, whisked and cooked 4 minutes, then added 1 package of shredded sharp cheddar, stirred until combined. Micro waved the broccoli in the packages while cooking the rice, then drained and added to a large bowl. fluffed the rice with a fork added to the broccoli, tossing until combined. Sprinkled the broccoli and rice with original Mrs. Dash, then poured the cheese mixture into the bowl gently tossing it all. Also I seasoned the onion and celery with a little salt and pepper as it was in the pan. Baked at 350 for 35 minutes. It is very good.
I added a pound of ground chicken that cooked with the onions and garlic with olive oil instead of butter. I layered the pan like a lasagna: rice, mixture, rice, mixture… it came out amazing!

I love it! Made it twice as it (reduced the celery, one whole bunch) I just made it for a third time with some changes just for variety. I minced a load of garlic and sautéed it with the veggies in butter. I only used 3 stalks of celery. And I seasoned the veggies while cooking with salt, pepper, blackening seasoning and just a dash of beef bouillon. Melted the velveeta and cream soups in the microwave, then mixed in! I also used 8 cups of cooked rice. The cheese sauce makes a lot! Also, using broccoli florets only, not "broccoli cuts" makes for a heartier and more attractive looking casserole. I may try to make a "Fiesta" version like another reviewer suggested!

Great side dish for a winter barbecue here in the South! Used fresh broccoli and par-cooked in microwave. One tsp onion powder, garlic powder each instead of sauté onions, omitted celery, added 1/4 tsp nutmeg. Also added 1 cup sour cream d/t used fat free cream of chicken and mushroom soups. Freshly grated Gouda and Sharp Cheddar cheeses each added to mixture. Used leftover Pepperidge Farm seasoned bread crumbs for topping w/ 3 T melted butter. Everyone enjoyed!

After sorting thru every broccoli and cheese recipe and reading all reviews I made this one. Every review was spot on. I used a 32 oz bag of broccoli thawed...not cooked tho...added a green pepper, mushrooms, and several of each color red orange and yellow mini peppers. Used brown rice and healthy choice/reduced fat soups (had to make it as diabetic friendly as possible). Cooked the veggies in olive oil not butter. It was runny going in but came out perfect. Made the 9x13 inch pan and one the size of a pie pan full. Will definitely make again. So yummy. Oh and yes def add some garlic or whatever your taste buds desire.

This recipe turned out really really great. I will send pictures. I used grapeseed oil and butter and instead of monster cheese I use provolone sharp cheddar cheese and white sharp cheddar cheese. Oh! I also used French fried onions instead of panko crumbs so good! Thank you!
great
It was okay, but probably wouldn't make it again.

Made it with all the ingredients listed but to expedite the process, I mixed all the ingredients together bypassing all the pre-cook instructions and added it to my casserole dish. I used fresh uncooked broccoli and added a can of sliced mushrooms and about 1/3 C of mayonnaise as well. Only used 2 C of brown rice. Mixed in the cheese and also topped it off with cheese and panko bread. I also added a good amount of curry powder, lemon pepper and cayenne for a little kick. Added alittle celery salt too. Baked it for 40 mins and it was bubbly hot and delicious!
I used fresh steamed broccoli!

This is the one! I have misplaced my recipe for B/R/C casserole and then found this. It is pretty much identical to my old one. Thank you for posting! I usually use cheddar, and occasionally use a different cream of soup, but I'm happy to actually have the recipe again.
More garlic and mustard, also added chopped Loma Linda Tender Bits. Used oaxaca cheese and a bit of parmesan. Cream of chicken with herbs soup. Was tasty but not extraordinary. Easy.
Great! I can't have sodium, so I used no-salt added canned creamed soups, and did not add any salt to the recipe. It came out delicious!
cream of celery instead of cream of mushroom
